chapters.title: The one animal we've never seen
What would you do if one grabbed you?
The first footage of a living colossal squid

title_pattern.template: Why You Never Want to Meet a [Creature]
title_pattern.notes: Second-person threat/avoidance framing ('you', 'never') turns a nature fact-file into a personal survival scenario. No number, no superlative in the title itself; the superlatives (heaviest invertebrate, biggest eyes) are saved for the hook and thumbnail. Same family as 'What If You Met a ...' / 'Why You Should Never ...'. The body pays it off with an explicit 'what would you do if one grabbed you' segment.

thumbnail.composition: Black background. Giant engraved/etched squid head fills the left two-thirds, its huge eye just left of centre is the focal point; hooked arms curl across the bottom edge. A tiny scuba diver with a torch beam sits mid-right, facing the eye. Text top-right.
thumbnail.text: IT SEES YOU.. (IT SEES in white, YOU.. in red), heavy geometric sans, all caps; red hand-drawn arrow from text curving into the eye.
thumbnail.colours: Near-monochrome black/white pen-and-ink stipple illustration; only accent is red (word YOU and arrow). Diver's torch beam is the brightest white.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Extreme: the diver is ~5% of frame height, the eye alone is ~6x the diver. The torch beam points straight at the eye, tying the two.
thumbnail.style_note: Thumbnail style (detailed engraving) is much more premium/creepy than the flat-vector video itself.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Single focal point (the eye) reinforced by arrow + text; 'YOU' in red makes it second-person and matches the title; scale contrast sells 'colossal' without a number; monochrome + one red accent pops in a colourful feed; the line implies a threat that is about to happen (curiosity gap: what happens to the diver).

hook.verbatim_0_to_16s: Picture this. It's the 21st century. We've filmed lions hunting at night, sharks breaching in slow motion, and whales giving birth in the open ocean. If an animal is big, we've seen it. Except one.
hook.verbatim_16_to_30s: The heaviest invertebrate on Earth lives in the ocean around Antarctica, and until very recently, nobody had ever filmed one alive in the deep. Not once. So, let's talk about why you'd never want to be the first.
hook.device: 'Picture this' second-person scene-setting + list-of-three of things we HAVE filmed (lion, breaching shark, whale) delivered as a fast montage, then a checklist grid of big animals all ticked green with one red '???' card: 'Except one.' Open loop / mystery gap (the one animal never filmed alive), reinforced by a fake ROV HUD with a 'LIVE ADULT COLOSSAL SQUID FILMED: 0' counter, then a title-callback pivot ('why you'd never want to be the first').
hook.visual_0_5s: Flat-vector ocean at sunset, small ship silhouette on the horizon, sun glitter on stylised wave lines (0-4 s); hard cut to stock lion-eating footage at ~4-5.7 s.

beats.summary: 'Picture this' - we've filmed lions, breaching sharks, whales giving birth; big-animal checklist grid all ticked except a red '???' card: 'Except one.'
Antarctica map, Southern Ocean; heaviest invertebrate never filmed alive in the deep; ROV HUD counter 'live adult filmed: 0'; title callback 'why you'd never want to be the first'.

What's scary in the ocean: sharks, orcas, giant squid - but you can see a shark coming, visit an orca at an aquarium, and the giant squid is 'spaghetti with opinions'. The colossal squid is different.
Giant vs colossal: longest vs heaviest/thickest/best armed; rope vs barrel; class-photo analogy (tall skinny kid vs the one who already has a beard); hero reveal title card with Latin name.
Sinking into the Southern Ocean: near-freezing water, sunlight gone by 200 m, none at 1,000 m; 'its zone' a few hundred to ~2,000 m.
2007 Ross Sea specimen ~half a ton = a grand piano 'with a beak'; biggest squid beak known; giant squid toothed suckers vs colossal arm hooks.
Swivel hooks on the tentacle clubs: if you twist to pull away the hook turns with you; fishing-lure analogy.

'No light - so how does it hunt?' Biggest eyes on Earth (~27 cm, bigger than a soccer ball, bigger than a blue whale's); 2012 study: eyes evolved to spot big animals' bioluminescent wake ~120 m away - it's watching for one thing.

What scares a half-ton squid? The sperm whale: deep dives, squid beaks piling up in stomachs, species described in 1925 from arm crowns in a whale stomach; whales return with circular scars - 'the only scorecard we have is the scars'.

'If one grabbed you, what would you do?' Five options list crossed off one by one: swim away (it sees you first), fight (2 arms vs 10 limbs - 'an argument with a ceiling fan'), pull free (swivel hooks), call for help (nearest rescue days away), hope it swallows you (donut brain, throat through the hole, beak cuts you into small pieces). Verdict: 'It would take its time.'

Hungry monster? Maybe not: 2010 metabolism study - ~30 g food/day (a slice of bread); one 5 kg fish lasts ~200 days; sit-and-wait predator - 'less shark, more the roommate who never leaves the couch'; scarier because it just needs you to come to it.

Humans meet them by accident: specimen timeline 1925/1981/2003; 2007 giant caught stealing an Antarctic toothfish (Chilean sea bass) off a longline; frozen and displayed at Te Papa; 2016 Ross Sea MPA 1.5M+ km2.

March 2025: Schmidt Ocean Institute ROV films a live juvenile ~30 cm at ~600 m, glass-clear, colour cells can switch clear/solid - 'basically invisible. Very reassuring.' 100 years after description; still zero adults filmed (HUD counter callback).
Food chain: eats fish, feeds sperm whales, sleeper sharks, seabirds; remove it and everything above feels it; whale scars callback - it keeps the biggest toothed predator fed.

Return to opening sunset ocean: we've mapped the planet and filmed almost everything; below Antarctica it floats in the dark watching for the glow of something big, unbothered that we're still looking.
Thanks for watching; comment which deep-sea creature next ('I do actually read them'); end screen with WATCH NEXT slot.

pacing.element_build_cadence_s: 2-4 (a label, tick, counter step or icon arrives roughly every sentence)
pacing.notes: Mostly continuous animated scenes on one dark-navy canvas with builds rather than cuts; stock footage inserts are short (2-5 s) literal illustrations of a spoken example. Narration is brisk and conversational with jokes every ~30-45 s. Chapters every ~1-1.5 min; the 'your options' segment (~75 s) is the longest single device.
pacing.shot_list_note: shot_list merges adjacent micro-shots (hook montage, detail sequences) to stay near 60 entries; finer visual changes ~every 6.6 s (scene-detect) with element builds every 2-4 s

techniques_worth_copying: Open-loop counter: a fake ROV HUD with 'LIVE ADULT ... FILMED: 0' in the cold open, reused at the payoff (8:50) - cheap code asset that carries the whole video's mystery.
Checklist grid with one red '???' card for 'we've seen every big animal except one' - instant visual for an exception.
Second-person survival segment as a game-style options menu (numbered list, highlight bar, strike-through as each option fails) - structures 75 s of content and boosts retention.

Concrete everyday scale comparisons rendered as simple props: balance scale vs grand piano, eye vs soccer ball/blue whale eye/hand, kitchen scale 30 g = slice of bread, tear-off calendar counting days.
Recurring callbacks of the same asset (swivel-hook-fish animation, scarred whale, sunset bookend) - saves production and rewards attention.
Paper-card citations (journal, year, title on a tilted cream card) - signals credibility in 3 s.
Jokey analogy scenes drawn crudely (class photo kids, stick figure vs ceiling fan, squid on the couch) every 30-45 s to break tension.
One-colour discipline: dark navy canvas, red squid/red accent text, white labels, cyan only for bioluminescence - consistent brand, easy in code.
Depth-descent shot: vertical ruler + counter + light shafts fading + caption steps (temperature, sunlight %) - reusable for any deep-sea topic.
Map zoom with red pin and caption chip for every place/date fact.
Thumbnail: monochrome engraved creature + tiny human + 3-word second-person text with one red word and a red arrow into the eye.
Twist reframe late in the video ('Hungry monster? ...maybe not') to re-hook before the history section.

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: High - ~85% of runtime is flat 2D vector animation on a dark canvas; the stock inserts (~45 s total) are literal illustrations that can be replaced by drawn scenes.
assets: SVG creature library in a consistent flat style: colossal squid (side, top-down crown, close-up eye, translucent juvenile variant), giant squid, sperm whale (side, diving, scarred head), fish/toothfish, shark, orca, other card icons

Prop SVGs: balance scale, grand piano, soccer ball, hand, kitchen scale, bread slice, tear-off calendar, specimen jar + shelf, menu card, paper citation card, phone, sofa + TV, ceiling fan, fishing boat + longline, ROV
Antarctica / world GeoJSON or simplified SVG path for map zooms, pins and MPA polygon
Engraving-style thumbnail art is the one piece that is hard in code - approximate with SVG hatching/stipple filters or a high-contrast line-art render
components: Dark-navy backdrop with drifting particle 'marine snow' and vignette (Canvas or SVG particles)
HUD overlay component (REC dot, timecode, crosshair, depth, counter box)
Card grid / card list with staggered pop-in and tick/X marks
Options-menu component with highlight bar and animated strike-through
Split-comparison layout with big numeric counters
Animated number counter (depth, beaks, days, years) with spring easing
Depth-descent scene: vertical ruler, light shafts with opacity by depth, caption steps
Map component with camera zoom/pan, pin drop, label chips, polygon draw-on
Timeline component (dots + red active state) and progress bar timeline
Line draw-on for scars, sight lines (dashed), callout brackets
Bioluminescent particle trail (cyan particles emitted along a path, fading)
Glowing eye (radial gradient + bloom) and iris/spotlight vignette transitions
Rubber-stamp text slam ('CAUGHT STEALING DINNER', '...MAYBE NOT')
Simple rigging for squid arms/tentacles (bezier wiggle) and hook rotation
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Local TTS narration (~170 wpm, conversational, wry), low ambient drone/music bed, subtle whooshes and pops on builds.
code_only_remake_requirements.typography: Heavy geometric sans (Montserrat/Poppins ExtraBold style) all-caps small labels, red underlined keywords; serif for paper/menu cards.
code_only_remake_requirements.timing_data: Drive builds from TTS word timestamps so each label lands on its spoken keyword.
